name: Postscript
description: Postscript is an SMS marketing and customer messaging platform for Shopify brands, with subscriber growth, keywords, campaigns, flows, two-way conversations, custom events, compliance, and webhook integrations.
agentUseSummary: Connect an enterprise or grandfathered API-enabled shop using its customer-owned private key. Relay pins 20 current v2 operations: six structural reads run directly, four subscriber/message reads and ten mutations require approval, and webhook signing-token retrieval plus partner shop-token impersonation remain blocked.

credentialRequirements.name: POSTSCRIPT_PRIVATE_API_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: Postscript shop private API key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use a dedicated shop private key from an enterprise/grandfathered API-enabled account; never use the public key.

capabilities.label: Read shop structure
capabilities.description: Use six bounded shop, keyword, and webhook metadata reads.

capabilities.label: Read subscribers and messages
capabilities.description: Use four bounded subscriber, message-request, and sent-message reads with approval.

capabilities.label: Manage SMS engagement
capabilities.description: Use ten compliance, messaging, event, subscriber, and webhook mutations with approval.

allowed.label: Read Postscript structure
allowed.description: Read exact shop identity, keywords, webhook subscriptions, and example event structure.

approvalRequired.label: Read subscribers or messages
approvalRequired.description: Read bounded subscriber, message-request, or sent-message data.

approvalRequired.label: Manage Postscript
approvalRequired.description: Send messages or events and manage subscribers, compliance, and webhooks.

blocked.label: Expose credentials
blocked.description: Private API keys, partner/shop tokens, webhook signing tokens, and authorization headers never enter agent-visible inputs or results.

blocked.label: Retrieve signing tokens
blocked.description: The webhook signing-token endpoint is credential lifecycle plumbing and is not agent-facing.

blocked.label: Impersonate another shop
blocked.description: Relay never accepts a dynamic X-Postscript-Shop-Token or routes a shop key under unrelated partner authority.

blocked.label: Use arbitrary or unbounded APIs
blocked.description: Only 20 pinned v2 operations run; legacy versions, arbitrary paths, origins, headers, pages, and oversized transfers are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Six structural reads run directly; all subscriber/message reads and ten mutations require approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: All 20 selected and shop-authorized operations run without Relay per-action approval; fixed routes, bounds, audits, provider compliance, and secret/impersonation blocks remain enforced.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts selected pinned Postscript v2 tools and attaches the encrypted shop private key server-side.

providerSetup.blocker: Postscript limits new custom shop API access to enterprise plans while grandfathered shops retain access; broader plan support requires an accepted integration partner and separate partner/shop tokens. No provider console or credential capture is allowed in this worker.
providerSetup.nextAction: Use an authorized enterprise/grandfathered shop or complete Postscript partner acceptance, create a dedicated private key, store it in Railway staging, and verify shop binding, reads, approval denial, compliant opt-in/send/unsubscribe/redact behavior, webhook lifecycle, rate limits, key revocation, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Postscript documents bearer authentication with private shop keys, optional partner plus X-Postscript-Shop-Token authority, and forbids use of public keys.
The current v2 reference publishes 21 endpoints across identity, compliance, events, keywords, messages, subscribers, and webhooks; Relay exposes 20 and blocks signing-token retrieval.
New custom shop API access is enterprise-only, grandfathered shops retain access, and accepted integration partners can serve shops on other plans using both partner and shop authority.
API-created subscribers must confirm opt-in and collection surfaces require TCPA-compliant language with linked terms and privacy notices.
Postscript documents a 15-request-per-second per-token or partner/shop-combination limit and 429 responses.
